content: This medication may cause mild side effects such as headache, back pain, or sinus and throat discomfort, which typically resolve within one to two days. It is important to understand that your doctor has prescribed this medication after determining that its benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, this medication can suppress your immune system, reducing your body’s ability to fight infections. As a result, you may become more susceptible to serious infections, including those affecting the lungs, bones, joints, skin, sinuses, or gastrointestinal system. Additionally, it may impair your ability to combat existing infections. If you experience any signs of infection, such as persistent nausea or vomiting, worsening redness, swelling, or tenderness at the injection site after two days, fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, painful or frequent urination, unusual vaginal discharge, burning, itching, or odor, or severe abdominal pain, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may also rarely cause a serious condition known as posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), which can be life-threatening. Furthermore, there is a small risk of developing cancer, including skin cancer, associated with this treatment. Discuss these risks and benefits thoroughly with your doctor. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you suspect an allergic reaction, seek medical attention immediately. This document does not list all possible side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. Some formulations may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex in the needle cover of prefilled syringes, which could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may increase your risk of infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid receiving immunizations or vaccinations without your doctor’s approval, and stay away from individuals who have recently received live vaccines, such as the oral polio vaccine or nasal flu vaccine. Additionally, avoid receiving BCG vaccines for one year after completing treatment with this medication. Take precautions to avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may pass into breast milk. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular medical and laboratory tests, such as skin exams, may be necessary. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
